data.name: Pine Springs Visitor Center
data.description: Pine Springs Visitor Center is the park's main visitor center and headquarters. Visitors can pay entrance and camping fees, tour the museum, purchase items from the park store, pick up brochures and maps, and obtain overnight wilderness use permits here.
data.passportStampLocationDescription: Passport stamp is located inside the visitor center.

passportStampImages.altText: A circle stamp with place name and date
passportStampImages.title: Guadalupe Mountains passport stamp

data.directionsInfo: Following US Hwy 62/180, you will see signs along the highway pointing you to our center. The visitor center is on the north side of the highway.

operatingHours.description: The Pine Springs Visitor Center is open year-round, closing on New Years Day, Thanksgiving Day, and Christmas Day.
operatingHours.name: Pine Springs Visitor Center

data.name: Dog Canyon Ranger Station
data.description: Visitors can pick up brochures and maps from the Dog Canyon Ranger Station when staff or volunteers are available. The Dog Canyon Ranger Station is open intermittently depending on staff availability. If staff and volunteers are present they may be patrolling trails or the campground and not necessarily inside the station.

passportStampImages.altText: A circle stamp with the location and date on it
passportStampImages.title: Dog Canyon passport stamp

data.directionsInfo: Coming from Texas: Traveling north on Highway 62/180 you will cross the state line into New Mexico. About 27 miles after crossing the state line, you will come up on the junction of Dark Canyon Rd-408. Turning in to Dark Canyon Rd-408 N follow the road for 22 miles to the junction of NM-137 N. At the junction, turn into NM-137 N and follow for 35 miles to the entrance of Dog Canyon.

operatingHours.description: The Dog Canyon Ranger Station is open intermittently depending on staff availability. Staff and volunteers may be in the area and not necessarily inside the station.
operatingHours.name: Dog Canyon Ranger Station

data.name: McKittrick Canyon Contact Station
data.description: Visit the contact station at the mouth of McKittrick Canyon (staffed during peak seasons in the spring and fall). Pick up a park brochure, and view the outside exhibits and video.
data.passportStampLocationDescription: Stamp is available when the visitor center is staffed.

passportStampImages.altText: A stamp circle with place and date
passportStampImages.title: McKittrick Canyon passport stamp

data.directionsInfo: Guadalupe Mountains National Park is located in far West Texas on U.S. Highway 62/180. The driving distance is 110 miles east of El Paso, Texas, 56 miles southwest of Carlsbad, New Mexico or 62 miles north of Van Horn on Hwy 54. The McKittrick Canyon access road is seven miles north of the Pine Springs visitor center. The McKittrick Canyon visitor center is at the end of the McKittrick Canyon access road.

operatingHours.description: McKittrick Canyon is open daily from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM Mountain Time. The gate at the highway is closed and locked at 5:00 PM. All visitors must be out of the area by 5:00 PM. The McKittrick Canyon Visitor Center restrooms are open daily. The trailhead is immediately through the breezeway. View the outside exhibits and video. The visitor center is open intermittently depending on staff availability.
operatingHours.name: McKittrick Canyon Visitor Center
